name: Nikias's Hoard
purpose: Colouring studio for multi-colour 3D printing: takes a finished single-colour print figure (STL) and gives every triangle one of a few colours (3-4 by default). Colour comes from a textured model of the same figure (OBJ, GLB, DAE, FBX, .blend), laid over the figure by itself and passed face by face when the shapes agree; or from reference pictures and textures read by the family's vision model, which chooses the palette, assigns a colour to each region of the figure (regions follow the folds where parts meet and the engraved lines), cuts finer the regions it finds mixed and corrects its own result after looking at it. A figure with no reference gets a picture of the character looked up on the web by its name and collection. Palettes are reduced in CIELAB; borders are straightened and patches under a share of the figure's size are absorbed, so it colours the same at any scale; regions, patches and brush spots can be repainted by hand. Writes painted 3MF for Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer and for PrusaSlicer, standard-colour 3MF, OBJ with one material per colour and the list of colours, also for the figure's flat and pivot variants; and a multicolour 3MF with one closed solid per colour (as parts for Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer, as volumes for PrusaSlicer, or standard 3MF), after checking and repairing the surface (open edges, normals, repeated faces, dust, loose pieces), with each separate piece also writable as its own STL. Assistants can browse the library, open figures, add and look at references, colour, look at the result from any side, repaint and export.

check.en: Open the 3MF in a slicer and check the colour regions, supports and reported geometry.
check.es: Abre el 3MF en el laminador y comprueba las zonas de color, los soportes y los avisos de geometría.

notes: library_scan lists the figures (query, group); project_create opens one and cuts it into regions. source_find proposes references by the figure's name in the user's folders and source_fetch looks the character up on the web; source_add takes a textured model, a picture or a folder and, for a model, says how well it fits the figure (fit under about 0.012 = same pose, colours pass directly; otherwise it is only a reference for the vision model). color_start mode auto|model|ai colours in the background (job_status); colors sets how many print colours; wish is free text for the vision model. figure_look what=clay|regions|color|compare|model|sources returns a picture from a named view, several views, a yaw/pitch or a close-up region [x, y, z, radius] in the figure's units; regions are numbered in the picture and those numbers are what paint regions takes. palette_set edits colours by position, count, merge [keep, remove], and base (colour 1); paint fills regions, patches around faces or brush spots; clean absorbs patches narrower than min_patch % of the figure's size; paint_undo takes back the last change. result_export writes into a Multicolor folder next to the figure; formats parts, parts-bambu and parts-prusa write one closed solid per colour (skin_depth in % of the figure's size, repair on by default, split also writes each separate piece as an STL). print_check says whether the figure is a closed, outward-facing solid and lists its loose pieces (repair: what the repair would leave). Palette indexes are 0-based (index 0 = colour 1, the object's own). Z is up.
